Sent: Monday, May 11, 2026 at 6:17 PM
From: "Amit Puri" <Mits@consultant.com>
To: ovation2.pm@delcondo.com
Cc: contact@ovation2board.ca, ovation2.admin@delcondo.com
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Chargeback Letter_Abell Pest Control_Unit 432

Good Morning,

I acknowledge receipt of your letter and the contents outlined by Management. However, acknowledgment of receipt does not constitute agreement with or acceptance of the concerns, conclusions, allegations, or liability asserted by the Corporation.

I have lived in this community for approximately 20 years and have maintained my home and livelihood here throughout that time. I have no interest in creating problems within the building or negatively impacting the community I have been part of for two decades. I ask that Management recognize that residents are individuals and not predetermined assumptions, accusations, or generalized character assessments. It is discouraging to feel that conclusions are being formed about my character or intentions without balanced consideration of my long-standing residency, cooperation, and efforts to resolve matters internally and respectfully.

I also note that I have been living in this community for two decades, while the current management appears relatively new. Changes in management or administration happen frequently in condominium communities, whether through acquisition, restructuring, or transition. However, long-term residents and their history within the community should still be given appropriate consideration and context when ongoing issues are being assessed.

With respect to the bed bug matter, I dispute Management’s position that I am responsible for treatment costs outside of my own unit. The allegation provided by a former unregistered occupant is unverified and appears to be relied upon without sufficient evidence. If the alleged infestation had truly existed continuously since September 2025, as claimed, then by the time of the February 2026 inspection there would reasonably have been a substantially more severe infestation throughout the surrounding areas and adjacent units. Instead, according to your own correspondence and contractor findings, only a limited number of bed bugs were identified within my unit and no infestation was confirmed in neighboring units following inspection and treatment.

I also have a recording of the inspector discussing the inspection findings, which I reserve the right to rely upon if necessary. Your own letter further confirms that no bed bugs were found in adjacent units after inspection. This raises serious questions regarding the basis for attempting to attribute broader building-related treatment costs to me.

Management has also confirmed in prior correspondence that neighboring units did not contain bed bugs following inspection. Despite this, Management still proceeded with spraying and broader treatment measures in surrounding areas while simultaneously attempting to assign the resulting costs to me. I do not understand the basis for imposing these additional expenses on me when your own records indicate that neighboring units were not found to have infestations. From my perspective, this creates unnecessary financial pressure and appears unreasonable. I intend to raise these concerns further through the appropriate channels if necessary.

It is difficult not to feel that Management is disproportionately relying on accusations and complaints made against me while giving insufficient consideration to statements and evidence from other residents who confirmed they had no bed bug concerns. Additionally, despite your confirmation that no neighboring infestations were found, Management still proceeded with wider treatment measures while continuing to insist that I bear responsibility for costs beyond my own unit.

I have repeatedly stated that I am willing to pay for reasonable treatment costs associated specifically with my own unit. However, preventative measures intended to protect the broader building, neighboring units, or common elements are a Corporation responsibility and should not automatically be transferred to a single owner absent clear evidence of negligence or direct causation.

Section 90(1) of the Ontario Condominium Act, 1998 states:

“Subject to section 91, the corporation shall maintain the common elements and each owner shall maintain the owner’s unit.”

Further, the suggestion that the presence of several bed bugs alone automatically establishes liability for all surrounding preventative measures is unreasonable, particularly where the source of introduction cannot be conclusively determined. Bed bugs may be transported from numerous external sources, including visitors, shared building spaces, deliveries, neighboring movement, or other environmental factors. Their presence alone does not establish fault.

I also continue to object to the repeated attempts to characterize this matter in a manner that appears accusatory and excessive despite my willingness to cooperate regarding my own unit treatment. The continued insistence that I must assume responsibility for broader costs without sufficient proof feels unreasonable and harassing.

Further, I dispute Management’s characterization that I failed to seek assistance or that reasonable interim solutions were properly made available to me.

I raised concerns regarding the damaged suite door and locking mechanism as early as December 2025. I also have recordings confirming that I repeatedly asked whether temporary repairs could be completed so that the locking mechanism would function safely while awaiting the replacement door. Management was fully aware of the condition of the door and possesses photographs documenting the damage.

Despite this, my requests for meaningful repair assistance were repeatedly declined or deferred. Management now states that solutions were offered, however this contradicts my direct communications and recordings. I specifically spoke with Mohamed, who acknowledged that temporary repair of the locking mechanism could potentially be done. This raises concern regarding inconsistent information being provided by Management representatives and leaves me uncertain as to who was providing accurate direction.

The door was significantly damaged on December 22, 2025, and Management was aware of the condition shortly thereafter. Accordingly, it is inaccurate to suggest that Management lacked notice of the issue or that no action could have been taken without a further report from me. Once Management became aware of a compromised suite entry door affecting safety and security, proactive steps should reasonably have been taken to address or stabilize the condition pending full replacement.

I will also be attaching photographs of the damaged locking mechanism for further clarity. Based on the visible condition of the mechanism, I request confirmation as to how soon temporary repairs could reasonably have been completed. This is especially important because Management previously advised me that temporary measures supposedly could not be performed and that full replacement was required, while other statements from Management representatives suggested temporary repairs may in fact have been possible.

I have consistently attempted to resolve matters within the community before escalating concerns externally. That is the responsible approach I believe residents should take. Unfortunately, I do not feel the same level of effort or fairness has been extended toward me, particularly where legal threats, allegations, or obligations have been asserted without what I consider sufficient notice, balanced investigation, or meaningful attempts at resolution.

Instead, the responsibility continued to be shifted back onto me while the unsafe and non-functioning condition persisted for months. I do not agree with the suggestion that Management fulfilled its obligations simply by advising me to wait for a custom replacement while the lock and security concerns remained unresolved.

With respect to the suite door issue, I will be making further inquiries with the appropriate local authorities regarding whether any compensation or responsibility may arise from the police-related incident and resulting damage.

To reiterate clearly:

  • I acknowledge receipt of your correspondence.

  • I do not acknowledge liability for broader preventative or neighboring treatment costs.

  • I remain willing to address reasonable charges relating specifically to treatment within my own unit.

  • I dispute the characterization that Management provided reasonable interim solutions regarding the suite door condition.

  • I reserve all rights regarding disputed charges, allegations, and future proceedings.

All future communications should remain in writing.

Regards,

Amit Puri

On 2026-05-08, 10:21 a.m. Ovation Ph II Management <Ovation2.pm@delcondo.com> wrote:
Good Morning Amit, 
We acknowledge receipt of your correspondence.
Management is somewhat puzzled by the concerns raised in your email, as many of the matters referenced have already been addressed through prior communications.
With respect to your suite entry door, please note that the final measurements for the replacement suite door were completed on March 28, 2026 by the contractor in attendance with Management. At that time, both the contractor and Management advised you that, as this is a custom-made door required to comply with the Corporation’s specifications and fire-rating requirements, the estimated manufacturing and delivery timeline would be approximately three (3) months, expected delivery is June on the exact date will be communicated from the contractor once available. This information was also communicated to you via email.
For clarity, the locking mechanism to the suite door of Unit 432 has been non-functioning since approximately June 2025. Management issued written notice to you in October 2025 advising that the lock was non-operational. This deficiency was observed during attended access to your unit with the Mississauga Fire Inspector, at which time Management was present and confirmed that the door hardware was not functioning properly.
Subsequently, the door sustained additional damage during the November 25, 2025 SWAT entry incident. In both instances, Management was not notified by you of the need for repairs. The deficiencies were identified by Management during inspection and official attendance, not through any service request initiated by you.
Please further note that the November 25, 2025 SWAT and police entry involved the arrest of an unregistered occupant residing within the unit, whom you had authorized to occupy the suite. Prior to this incident, Management had already communicated concerns regarding unregistered occupants and rooming accommodations on November 20, 2025, as well as again on November 25, 2025.
You were present during the police and SWAT attendance and therefore may have a better understanding of the circumstances leading to the raid and arrest. With respect to your inquiry regarding authorization of the entry, please be reminded that the attendance and actions taken were carried out by police and SWAT authorities pursuant to their own legal authority and procedures. Any inquiries regarding the police operation, authorization, or enforcement actions should be directed to the appropriate local authorities.
You may also wish to make inquiries directly with the occupant whom you authorized to reside within the unit regarding why they were questioned or arrested by authorities. This matter is outside of Management and the Board’s control and jurisdiction.
Please be advised that Section 40(f) of the Corporation’s Declaration – Maintenance and Repairs to the Common Elements – states:
“Each owner shall forthwith reimburse the Corporation for the cost of repairs made by the Corporation to any windows, skylights and/or doors serving his or her dwelling unit, following damage to same caused by such owner's negligence or wilful misconduct, or caused by the negligence or wilful misconduct of the residents, tenants, invitees or licensees of his or her unit (or by anyone else for whose actions such owner is responsible, at law or in equity), and where the cost of rectifying any such damage is recoverable under any policy of insurance held or maintained by the Corporation, then the owner responsible for such damage as aforesaid shall forthwith reimburse the Corporation for the deductible amount paid or payable under such insurance policy.”
Further, in several of your email communications, you have stated that you were allegedly unable to leave the unit due to the door condition. However, Management had previously advised both you and your brother-in-law that the door lock could be replaced independently while awaiting the new door installation. Management provided the required lock replacement forms to both you and your brother-in-law by email and hard copy for completion should you wish to proceed with replacement of the malfunctioning lock.
At that time, you advised the Management Office that you preferred to wait until the replacement door arrived rather than proceed with the interim lock replacement. Nevertheless, on April 30, 2026, Management received a further inquiry from you regarding the lock. Management again responded advising that you could complete and submit the lock replacement form so the lock replacement could proceed and permit secure locking of the unit. To date, Management has not received the completed form from you.
Please further note that the locking mechanism will require replacement apart from installation of the new door. The replacement cost for the lock is $317.53 (HST included). The form is re-attached for your reference and should you wish to proceed with replacement, kindly have the form filled out and emailed back for processing and scheduling.
Please note that suite entry doors are common element components and must comply with the Corporation’s specifications, including fire-rating requirements, alignment, hardware standards, and uniform appearance throughout the building. Accordingly, all repairs and replacement work must be carried out exclusively by contractors retained or approved by the Corporation. Since the door and related requirements are custom-made and manufactured specifically to the measurements taken by the manufacturer, production timelines do require additional time. Although the contractor informed you of this information during the final inspection, Management is therefore unclear as to why you have referenced a five-month delay when you were advised both verbally and by email that the estimated timeline was approximately three (3) months from April 2026.
With respect to the bed bug matter, Management received a complaint on February 3, 2026 from a prior, unregistered occupant of Unit 432 alleging the presence of bed bugs dating back to September 2025. The complainant advised that they had informed you of the issue prior to vacating the unit few days after their stay in September, 2025. 
Given the seriousness of the complaint and the Corporation’s obligations under the Condominium Act, 1998 and the Corporation’s Rules, Management immediately retained Abell Pest Control, a licensed pest control contractor, to investigate the matter. An inspection was conducted on February 6, 2026, which confirmed the presence of bed bugs within Unit 432. The contractor identified a total of eight (8) live bed bugs during the inspection, which constitutes an active infestation requiring immediate treatment. It only takes one bedbug to produce 200 to 500 eggs in its lifetime. 
Management’s records confirm that no report or notice regarding a possible infestation was submitted by you to the Management Office between September 2025 and February 2026.
The contractor’s report further confirmed that no bed bugs were found in the adjacent units inspected after inspection and treatment of adjacent units and above. The live bed bugs identified during the inspection were found only within Unit 432 during inspection.
Management would also like to note that during the second treatment carried out on March 17, 2026, the condition of the unit was observed to be unsafe and unclean. Please be reminded that unit owners are required to ensure that their unit is maintained in a sanitary condition and that no infestation or presence of pests, insects, rodents, or other vermin is permitted or suffered within the unit.
As previously communicated, Section 21 of the Corporation’s Rules states:
“No unit owner shall permit or suffer the infestation of his or her unit (or any exclusive use common element area with respect thereto) by pests, insects, rodents, or other vermin. Failure to comply with the foregoing, or the failure to report such infestation to the Board as soon as the owner is aware of same, will render such owner liable for all costs and expenses incurred by the Corporation in eradicating such infestation from other units and/or common elements.”
Accordingly, pursuant to the Corporation’s Rules, as the unit owner you have rendered yourself liable for all costs and expenses incurred by the Corporation in eradicating the infestation from other units and/or common elements. Therefore, your unit remains responsible for all related costs rendered by the Corporation in connection with this matter.
With respect to your comments regarding the balcony structure and possible pest entry, Management notes that you were previously contacted regarding the cleanliness and condition of the balcony area of suite 432. Management observed garbage bags, tires, and other unauthorized items stored on the balcony. Multiple notices were issued requesting compliance; however, the concerns remained unresolved, resulting in legal correspondence being issued to you on July 29, 2025 directing that the balcony be maintained in proper order and that items not be stored on the balcony except for seasonal furniture and permitted items. A second legal letter was issued on March 29, 2026 for the same issue. 
Despite the legal notices, Management continued to observe non-compliance and improper storage conditions on the balcony. Please be reminded that poor housekeeping and accumulation of garbage or stored items may contribute to pest-related concerns.
However, for clarity, the infestation identified and treated in this matter involved bed bugs treatment, not exterior pests entering through the balcony structure.
Accordingly, pursuant to the Corporation’s Rules, as the unit owner you have rendered yourself liable for all costs and expenses incurred by the Corporation in eradicating the infestation from other units and/or common elements. Therefore, your unit remains responsible for all related costs rendered by the Corporation in connection with this matter.
Based on the foregoing, the Corporation’s position remains that the failure to report and address the infestation in a timely manner, as well as the damages sustained to the suite entry door arising from the actions of occupants authorized by you to reside within the unit, constitute breaches of the Corporation’s governing documents and render the unit owner responsible for the associated costs.
Please also note that Management and the Board categorically deny any allegation of harassment, discrimination, bad faith, or improper conduct. Management Office on behalf of The Corporation has acted in accordance with its obligations under the Condominium Act, 1998 and the governing documents of the Corporation, with the objective of protecting the health, safety, and welfare of all residents.
Should you wish to propose a payment plan for the Board’s consideration, you may do so in writing. Any proposal should include a suggested repayment structure for the current outstanding charges as well as future charges and pending invoices, including the suite entry door replacement. Please be advised that the replacement cost of the suite entry door is $3,591.00 + HST.
All future communications regarding this matter or any other matter should continue to be provided in writing.
 

Kind Regards,

Dear Board Members and Property Management,

I am writing to formally dispute the bed bug–related charges issued against me, including charges relating to adjacent units, and to escalate serious concerns regarding harassment, unsupported allegations, procedural unfairness, prolonged maintenance failures, security concerns, and possible legal infractions.

Please treat this correspondence as formal notice that I do not accept these charges.

I request the official process for disputing these charges, including all required procedures, documentation requirements, and timelines. I also request that all collection activity or enforcement related to these disputed charges be immediately suspended pending proper review and investigation.

Despite previous communications requesting clarification and evidence, no documentation has been provided establishing that my unit was the source of any infestation or that I am legally responsible for the costs imposed.

The inspection findings referenced only two dead bed bugs within my unit, which is consistent with incidental transfer rather than an originating infestation. At no point did the inspector’s written findings identify my unit as the source or confirm spread from my unit to adjacent units.

I further place on record that I possess video-recorded conversations and evidence involving neighbours and discussions surrounding the inspection process, which do not support the conclusion that my unit was the source of any infestation.

The inspector also did not write or conclude that my unit was the source.

Accordingly, I object to any attempt to impose financial responsibility based on assumptions, hearsay, or unverified accusations.

Unverified allegations alone do not constitute a reasonable or lawful basis for chargeback, particularly where:

  • No direct evidence establishes origin or causation
  • No written inspection finding identifies my unit as the source
  • No procedural fairness or evidentiary standard has been demonstrated
  • Adjacent-unit costs are being assigned without proof of spread from my unit

I formally request clarification regarding how management determined that I am financially responsible for treatment costs affecting multiple units.

I also reiterate that external factors remain possible. My balcony structure is not sealed or cemented in the same manner as other balconies, creating a possible entry point for pests from outside. These structural conditions should have been considered before assigning liability.

I also raise serious concerns regarding the condition and handling of my unit door.

My unit door has remained damaged and unresolved for approximately five months. Over my many years of residence in this community, different contractors have regularly been used for maintenance and repairs. However, I am now being told that only one contractor can perform this replacement, resulting in unreasonable delay.

I spoke directly with Mohammed, identified to me as board president, who acknowledged that five months is an excessive timeframe and indicated that temporary repairs could be arranged pending contractor availability. Despite this, no proper interim solution has been implemented.

This prolonged delay compromises my safety, security, and living conditions.

In addition, I request a full explanation regarding how and why my unit door was broken into, including:

  • Who authorized the entry
  • Under what legal authority it occurred
  • What notice was provided to me
  • Whether incident reports, contractor records, or board authorizations exist regarding this incident

The lack of clarity surrounding this matter raises serious concerns regarding unauthorized access, procedural violations, and resident safety.

I am also placing on record that the manner in which this matter has been handled has caused significant distress and hardship. The repeated pressure, unsupported allegations, financial burdens, and lack of procedural fairness have created an overwhelming situation for me and my family during an already difficult time following my father’s passing.

My father experienced significant stress as a result of the financial and emotional pressure associated with these matters, and I continue to seek clarity and accountability regarding how these circumstances were allowed to escalate in this manner.

I have lived within this condominium community for approximately 20 years, paid my dues, maintained my residence, and never previously experienced complaints or conflict. My circumstances changed significantly following my stroke, after which I became dependent on CPP Disability support.

Given these circumstances, I am concerned that I may be experiencing unfair or disproportionate treatment. If disability-related vulnerability or financial limitations are being used against me, directly or indirectly, this raises serious concerns regarding fairness, accommodation, and equal treatment obligations.

The circumstances described above may constitute breaches of the , including:

  • Section 17(3) – Duty of the corporation to manage and administer the property honestly and in good faith
  • Section 37 – Duty of care and diligence by directors and officers
  • Section 89 – Requirement that chargebacks and indemnification be reasonable and properly supported

The circumstances may also raise concerns under the , including:

  • Section 1 – Equal treatment with respect to occupancy of accommodation
  • Section 2 – Protection from discriminatory treatment in housing-related matters

I further question:

  • The authority under which these charges were issued
  • Whether these charges were formally approved by the board
  • Why inconsistent explanations regarding contractors and procedures have been provided

I hereby request the following within 5 business days:

  1. Immediate suspension of all disputed charges and collection activity pending investigation
  2. All evidence supporting the allegation that my unit is the source
  3. Evidence supporting liability for adjacent units
  4. Full pest control and inspection reports
  5. Documentation authorizing the chargeback
  6. Clarification regarding the forced entry/break-in incident involving my door
  7. Written timeline for temporary and permanent repair of my door
  8. Information regarding the condominium’s formal dispute resolution process
  9. Clarification regarding who specifically authorized and issued these charges

Until proper evidence and documentation are provided, I do not accept responsibility for these charges.

If this matter is not addressed promptly and fairly, I intend to proceed with further escalation through the Condominium Authority of Ontario, the Human Rights Tribunal of Ontario, and additional legal and regulatory channels as necessary.

I request that all future communication regarding this matter be provided in writing.

Sincerely,

Amit Puri

subject: Fw: Bank draft for elevator withheld
body:
Sent: Thursday, April 02, 2026 at 8:22 AM
From: "Amit Puri" <Mits@consultant.com>
To: contact@ovation2board.ca
Subject: Bank draft for elevator withheld
Dear Sir/Madam,
 
I am writing to formally raise a complaint against the property manager regarding ongoing conduct that constitutes harassment, misuse of authority, and clear violations of the Condominium Act, 1998.
 
Firstly, my elevator booking was properly secured with a bank draft, and building security fully cleared the use without issue. However, the property manager has refused to return or process the bank draft, claiming it was “dirty,” which is not a valid or recognized reason under any condominium rule or policy. The draft is now being retained for alleged “cleaning purposes” without inspection, documentation, or due process. This raises serious concerns regarding improper financial conduct and lack of transparency.
 
Secondly, I am in the process of removing items from my unit and balcony due to a suspected bed bug issue. The temporary condition is directly related to remediation. Despite full awareness of this, the property manager escalated the matter by issuing legal notices and demanding payments. This is excessive, unreasonable, and punitive.
I have also received legal correspondence demanding payment while I am actively resolving the issue. This creates undue financial pressure and appears coercive.
 
Additionally, I have been waiting approximately four (4) months for a door replacement, with further delays of two (2) months now indicated. This ongoing delay has affected my safety and living conditions. The damage itself arose in a context involving prior complaints and miscommunication by property management and security.
 
I am currently recovering from a brain stroke and have limited financial capacity. Despite this, I am being subjected to escalating financial demands, restrictive actions, and what appear to be improper fines, placing me at risk of housing instability.
 
I made reasonable efforts to maintain the premises and requested basic assistance (such as maintenance tools to clean debris), which were denied. Instead, enforcement and legal pressure have increased.
 
Legal Infractions and Breaches
The conduct described above appears to violate multiple provisions of the Condominium Act, 1998, including:
Section 17(3) – The corporation has a duty to take reasonable steps to ensure compliance with the Act, declaration, by-laws, and rules. Selective or punitive enforcement fails this obligation.
Section 37(1) – Directors and officers (including agents such as property managers) must act honestly, in good faith, and exercise reasonable care and diligence. The actions described reflect a failure to meet this standard.
 
Section 119 – Owners are required to comply with rules; however, enforcement must be reasonable, consistent, and not arbitrary. The current actions appear selective and disproportionate.
 
Section 134 – Compliance and enforcement actions (including legal steps) must be reasonable and justified. Escalating to legal notices under these circumstances may constitute abuse of this provision.
 
Section 135 – Oppression remedy: conduct that is oppressive, unfairly prejudicial, or unfairly disregards the interests of an owner. The pattern of financial pressure, delays, and selective enforcement may meet this threshold.
Additionally, the handling of funds (bank draft retention without basis) raises concerns regarding fiduciary responsibility and proper financial practices expected of condominium management.
 
Requested Resolution
 
I respectfully request: Immediate return or proper accounting of the elevator bank draft Withdrawal or review of any legal demands or financial penalties issued Immediate action and confirmed timeline for door replacement Formal investigation into the property manager’s conduct Reasonable accommodation given my medical and financial circumstances
 
I have made multiple attempts to resolve this matter informally, including discussions with management representatives, but no resolution has been achieved.
 
If this matter is not addressed promptly, I will escalate to appropriate regulatory authorities and pursue all available remedies, including under Section 135 (oppression).

I

Dear PSC 764 Management and Members of the Board,

Thank you for your email..

I am writing to formally request that this matter be placed before the Board for discussion at a Board meeting, or that a Board meeting be convened promptly to address and confirm resolution.

This request is made further to my in-person verbal conversation with Mr. Muhammad, a Board member, who confirmed that the charge would be withdrawn.

A Board meeting and written confirmation will ensure clarity, proper governance, and an accurate record of the Board’s decision.

I acknowledge Management’s clarification regarding its communications and confirm that I have fully complied with the request to cease roommate activity.

Compliance was achieved promptly upon notice, and no legal enforcement action was required.

I remain in compliance with the Corporation’s Declaration, By-laws, and Rules and will continue to do so in accordance with Section 119 of the Condominium Act, 1998.

In addition, principles of procedural fairness require that enforcement be reasonable, proportionate, and based on actual necessity.

Where an owner is provided notice and brings themselves into compliance, fairness and the Act do not permit the imposition of charges in the absence of real enforcement costs.

It is also important to note that the ordinary and regular duties of property management, including monitoring compliance, corresponding with owners, and advising the Board, form part of Management’s contracted responsibilities and do not constitute chargeable compliance costs.

Routine administrative functions cannot be converted into owner chargebacks.

Under the Condominium Act, 1998, condominium corporations are not authorized to levy fines or penalties.

While Section 17(3) obligates the corporation to enforce its governing documents, enforcement must occur in accordance with the Act.

Further, Section 134 permits recovery only of actual costs incurred in obtaining compliance (including legal costs, where applicable), and does not authorize penalties, preset fees, or administrative charges unrelated to actual expenses.

Any chargeback to an owner must therefore be limited to actual, reasonable, and documented compliance-related costs, incurred only after proper notice and an opportunity to comply, as contemplated by Sections 119 and 134 of the Act.

In this case:

  • Sufficient notice was provided,

  • I complied within that notice period,

  • No legal action under Section 134 was commenced,

  • No documented compliance-related costs were incurred, and

  • I am now in compliance with all alleged infractions.

Accordingly, no valid charge arose from the alleged non-compliance, and the $500 administrative charge is invalid and unenforceable and must be removed in full.

As the charge does not reflect actual expenses incurred by the Corporation, it constitutes an unlawful penalty, regardless of how it is described in the Rules.

I respectfully request written confirmation that:

  • The charge has been withdrawn, and

  • My account reflects a $0 balance in relation to this matter.

For clarity, I would also appreciate an explanation regarding the deactivation of one of the unit’s fobs.

As Management has indicated that no specific direction was issued requiring the removal of occupants, it is unclear on what basis the fob was deactivated.

I respectfully request clarification as to how this action aligned with the stated compliance request and applicable procedures.

Additionally, I note an inconsistency in the characterization of the charge.

Earlier correspondence referred to a “non-registration fee,” whereas later communications describe the amount as an “administrative fee.”

I would appreciate clarification on this point, as a change in terminology does not alter the underlying legal requirement that any charge must reflect actual, documented costs.

Please also note that a separate communication will be provided by my team addressing other occupancy-related issues for review and discussion.

This letter is limited solely to the charge addressed above.

I respectfully reiterate my request that this matter be addressed and confirmed at a Board meeting, consistent with my verbal discussion with Mr. Muhammad, and that written confirmation of the Board’s decision be provided for the record.

Sincerely,

Amit Puri

Dear Victor,
 
I am writing to formally raise concerns regarding the conduct of your office and its handling of my condominium matter related to PSCC 754, Unit 432 at 3888 Duke of York Blvd.
 
First, I must express my disappointment with the misbehaviour and unprofessionalism of your office’s reception staff. My repeated attempts to contact your office to resolve this issue have been ignored. Calls go unanswered, and your receptionist refuses to provide any helpful information or direct communication. This lack of transparency and accessibility is unacceptable and contrary to the professional standards expected of a law office.
 
It also appears that your firm has been engaging in unnecessary legal actions over an issue that could have been resolved directly between myself and the property management. This conduct has caused me significant distress and financial burden. I have always been a responsible owner and have never missed a condominium payment in over 15 years. I have also been informed that your firm intends to place a lien on my unit. I need written clarification of the lien protocol, specifically:
 
Does the lien amount remain fixed at the time of registration, or does it continue to accumulate interest and legal fees after filing?
 
How are interest and administrative costs calculated once a lien is registered?
 
What exact steps must I take to pay the amount in full and return the account to good standing?
 
 
In addition, I would like clarification regarding the ownership and maintenance responsibilities of balconies under the condominium’s declaration. When I purchased my unit, the large balcony was a key selling feature — it was presented as an exclusive-use area belonging to the owner. However, I have since been subjected to multiple disturbing incidents, including being spat on, having vomit and dangerous objects thrown down, and experiencing flooding and fire hazards due to the balcony’s design and exposure. Despite numerous complaints over the years, management has failed to take any protective or corrective actions.
 
Please clarify:
 
Are balconies considered exclusive-use common elements or unit owner property?
 
If the balcony is a common element, why has the condominium corporation not ensured safety or cleanliness, despite repeatedly accessing my balcony without notice?
 
 
Your firm’s involvement — combined with management’s lack of accountability — has made it impossible to resolve these issues reasonably. Given these ongoing problems, I want to make it clear that I will be filing a formal complaint with the Law Society of Ontario regarding your firm’s conduct, billing practices, and failure to communicate appropriately with a unit owner acting in good faith.
 
Please provide the following within 10 business days:
 
1. A complete statement of account detailing all legal, administrative, and interest charges.
 
 
2. A copy of the lien notice and all related documentation.
 
 
3. Written confirmation of the process to pay the original condominium amount directly to the corporation.
 
 
4. Clarification on balcony ownership as per the condominium’s governing documents.
 
 
 
I expect professional cooperation and transparency in resolving this matter. I am also forwarding this correspondence to the District Property Manager for awareness and potential intervention.
 
Please respond by email or call me directly at 647-717-0929 to arrange a resolution.
 
Sincerely,
Amit Puri

3888 Duke of York Blvd
Mississauga, ON
